record.paper_title: Using GANs for Sharing Networked Time Series Data: Challenges, Initial Promise, and Open Questions
record.original_question: When a synthetic data generator models both per-sample attributes and associated time-series records, how can practitioners realistically tune the attribute distributions of the released synthetic dataset while still preserving the conditional behavior between those attributes and the generated records?

evidence.quote: A major open question is how to realistically tune attribute distributions.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{D} = \{(a_i, x_i)\}_{i=1}^N$ be a dataset where each sample consists of an attribute vector $a_i \in \mathcal{A}$ (e.g., categorical or numerical metadata) and an associated time-series record $x_i \in \mathcal{X} = \mathbb{R}^{T \times d}$. Suppose a generative model has been trained to produce joint synthetic samples $(A, X)$ approximating the joint distribution $P(A, X) = P(A)\,P(X \mid A)$ of real data, where $P(A)$ is the marginal attribute distribution and $P(X \mid A)$ is the conditional distribution of time series given attributes.

A data publisher wishes to release synthetic data whose marginal attribute distribution matches a chosen target distribution $Q(A)$ (which may differ from the empirical $P(A)$, for instance to anonymize, rebalance rare categories, or correct sampling bias), while preserving the learned conditional behavior $P(X \mid A)$ between attributes and records.

Design and analyze a principled procedure that, given:
(i) a generator $G$ producing samples from $P(A, X)$,
(ii) a desired target attribute distribution $Q(A)$,

outputs a synthetic dataset $\widetilde{\mathcal{D}}$ whose attribute marginal converges (in a specified statistical sense, e.g., total variation or Wasserstein distance) to $Q(A)$ and whose conditional law $\widetilde{P}(X \mid A)$ remains close to the original $P(X \mid A)$. Specifically:

1. Formulate sufficient conditions on $G$, on $Q(A)$, and on the relationship between $Q(A)$ and the support of $P(A)$ under which such a procedure is well-defined and statistically consistent.
2. Provide quantitative bounds relating any divergence $D(Q \| P)$ on attributes to the achievable fidelity of the conditional $\widetilde{P}(X \mid A)$ versus $P(X \mid A)$.
3. Characterize fundamental obstructions (e.g., when $Q$ places mass on attribute regions poorly covered by training data) and propose diagnostics that detect when realistic tuning is infeasible.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of realistically tuning attribute marginals in conditional generative models for networked/time-series data while preserving learned conditional structure remains an active research area. Subsequent work on DoppelGANger and conditional tabular/time-series GANs (e.g., CTGAN, follow-up DoppelGANger studies) discuss attribute conditioning and rebalancing, but a general principled methodology with consistency guarantees for arbitrary target attribute distributions has not been established, so the question is best characterized as still open.

status_evidence.title: Using GANs for Sharing Networked Time Series Data
status_evidence.snippet: Identifies realistic tuning of attribute distributions as a major open question for synthetic networked time-series data.
status_evidence.claim: The originating discussion lists this as an explicitly open challenge.

status_evidence.title: DoppelGANger and follow-ups on conditional time-series GANs
status_evidence.snippet: Subsequent works extend conditional generation and attribute control but do not provide a general consistent procedure for arbitrary target attribute marginals with conditional preservation guarantees.
status_evidence.claim: No comprehensive solution has been published; methods remain heuristic.
